Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 1:

(p-321) Surat "Muhammad" (ﷺ)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Those who disbelieve and bar [others] from the way of Allah﴾: that is, they turned away and refrained from entering Islam, or they barred others from it. Al-Jawhari said: "ṣadda ʿanhu, yaṣudd, ṣudūdan" means he turned away; and "ṣaddahu ʿan al-amr, ṣaddan" means he prevented him from it and diverted him away from it. They are the ones who fed [people] on the day of Badr, or the People of the Book, or it is general, covering everyone who disbelieved and barred [others].

﴿He has caused their deeds to go astray﴾: He nullified them and rendered them void. Its essential meaning is making them lost and wasted, with no one to accept them and reward them for them, like a strayed camel. "Their deeds" refers to what they did in their disbelief, such as maintaining family ties, feeding guests, and tending the Sacred Mosque, or what they did of plotting against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and barring [others] from the way of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 2:

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾: they are a group of people from Quraysh, or from the Ansar, or from the People of the Book, or the expression is general.

﴿And believed in what was sent down upon Muhammad﴾: that is the Qur'an. The singling out of belief in what was sent down to His Messenger from among all that must be believed in is to magnify his status. He emphasized this with the parenthetical clause, which is His saying: ﴿and it is the truth from their Lord﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. It is also said that the religion of Muhammad is the truth, since abrogation does not apply to it, while it abrogates other religions.

﴿He will remove from them their misdeeds﴾: by their belief and their righteous deeds, He will cover over what they had of disbelief and sins, because of their turning away from them and their repentance.

﴿And will amend their condition﴾: i.e., their state and their affairs, by granting them success in matters of the religion, and by empowering them over the world through the victory and support He gave them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 3:

﴿That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord.﴾ "That" (ذَلِكَ, dhalika) is a subject (mubtada'), and what follows it is its predicate (khabar), i.e.: "That matter — which is the misguidance of the deeds of one of the two groups, the expiation of the evil deeds of the second, and the setting right (of their affairs) — is due to the fact that these follow falsehood, which is Satan, and those follow the truth, which is the Qur'an."

﴿Thus﴾, like that manner (ḍarb),

﴿Allah sets forth﴾, i.e., Allah makes clear,

﴿for mankind their parables﴾. The pronoun (ḍamīr) refers either to "mankind" or to the two groups mentioned, in the sense that He sets forth their parables for the sake of mankind, so that they may take heed by them. He has made following falsehood a parable for the deeds of the disbelievers, and following the truth a parable for the deeds of the believers. Or He has made misguidance a parable for the failure of the disbelievers, and the expiation of evil deeds a parable for the success of the righteous.

﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve﴾: from "al-liqa'" (meeting), which means war.

﴿then [it is] striking of the necks﴾: the original form is "fa-idribu al-riqab darban" (so strike the necks with a strike). The verb was omitted and the verbal noun (masdar) was placed first, taking its position, and is made a construct with its object. This involves brevity while conveying emphasis, because you mention the verbal noun and it indicates the verb through the force of the act it contains. "Darb al-riqab" (striking of the necks) is an expression for killing. It does not mean that one must strike specifically the necks and not other limbs, but because killing a person most often occurs by striking his neck, it became an expression for killing, even if one strikes other than the neck.

﴿until when you have subdued them﴾: you have increased the killing among them.

﴿then tighten the bonds﴾: then take them captive. "Al-wathaq" (the bond), with a fatha or a kasra, is the name of that with which one is bound. The meaning is: tighten the bonds of the captives, so that they do not escape from you.

﴿then either [release them as] a favour afterwards﴾: that is, after you have taken them captive.

﴿or [take] ransom﴾: "manan" (a favour) and "fida'an" (ransom) are both in the accusative, governed by verbs implied for each of them. That is: "either you bestow a favour, or you ransom [them] with a ransom." The meaning is a choice between the two matters after capture: between bestowing a favour on them so that you release them, and between ransoming them.

According to us, the ruling on captives from among the polytheists is: execution, or enslavement. The favour and ransom mentioned in the verse are abrogated (mansukh) by His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5], because Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah) is among the last things revealed. It is related from Mujahid: "Today there is no favour nor ransom; there is only Islam or the striking of the neck." Or the intended meaning of the favour is that a favour is bestowed on them by sparing them from killing and they are enslaved, or a favour is bestowed on them so that they are released in return for their acceptance of the jizya (poll tax). And by ransom is meant that prisoners of the Muslims are ransomed in exchange for their prisoners. This was transmitted by al-Tahawi as the school of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is the view of the two of them (Abu Yusuf and al-Shaybani). The well-known position is that he does not permit their ransom, neither with wealth nor with anything else, lest they return to be a war against us. According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him: the ruler may choose one of four matters: execution, enslavement, ransom in exchange for Muslim prisoners, and favour.

﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾: its loads, and its instruments on which it cannot stand except by them, such as weapons and the horses (kura'). It was said: "its burdens" means its sins; that is, "until the people of war, who are the polytheists, abandon their polytheism by embracing Islam." Or [the meaning is that] "until" necessarily relates either to the striking and tightening, or to the favour and ransom. The meaning on both connections according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, is that they will remain in that state forever, until there is no war with the polytheists, and that is when they no longer have any power. It was said: [it is] when Isa, peace be upon him, descends. According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him: if it is connected to the striking and tightening, the meaning is that they are killed and taken captive until the war in its genus lays down its burdens, and that is when the polytheists no longer have any power. If it is connected to the favour and ransom, the meaning is that a favour is bestowed on them and they are ransomed until the war of Badr lays down its burdens, unless the favour and ransom are interpreted in the manner we have mentioned.

﴿That [is so]﴾: the matter is that, so it is a subject and predicate; or: do that to them, so it is in the accusative position.

﴿And had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them﴾: He would have exacted retribution from them without fighting, by some means of destruction, such as swallowing by the earth, or an earthquake, or other than that.

﴿but [He ordered you to fight]﴾ to be the one who commanded you to fight.

﴿so that He may test some of you by means of others﴾: that is, the believers by means of the disbelievers, as a purification for the believers and an annihilation for the disbelievers.

﴿And those who were killed﴾: Basri and Hafs [read it as] "qutilu" (were killed); the others [read it as] "qatalu" (fought).

﴿in the way of Allah, He will never waste their deeds﴾

(p-324) ﴿He will guide them﴾ to the path of Paradise, or to the right answer to the questions of Munkar and Nakir (the two angels who question the dead in their graves),

﴿and will set their minds at ease﴾: He will satisfy their adversaries (khusama'), and will accept their deeds.

﴿And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.﴾ From Mujahid: "He made known to them their dwellings therein, so that they would not need to ask [anyone for directions]." Or [the meaning is] that He perfumed it for them, from "al-'Arf" (ʿarf), which is pleasant fragrance.

O you who believe, if you help Allah (i.e., the religion of Allah and His Messenger),

He will help you (ينصركم) against your enemy, and grant you victory (ويفتح لكم),

and make your feet firm (ويثبت أقدامكم) in the places of battle, or upon the clear path (محجة) of Islam.

Surah 47, verse 8 — Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿And those who disbelieve﴾: it is in the nominative position as the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate (khabar) is ﴿then stumbling for them﴾. He conjoined his statement ﴿and He has caused their deeds to go astray﴾ to the verb that put "ta'san" (stumbling) in the accusative, because the meaning is: "so He said: stumbling for them." "Al-ta's" means "al-'uthur" (stumbling, falling down).

And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "He means in the world, killing; and in the Hereafter, falling headlong into the Fire."

**﴿That﴾**, i.e., the ruin and misguidance,

**﴿because they hated what Allah has sent down﴾**, i.e., the Qur'an,

**﴿so He made their deeds fruitless﴾**

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 10:

﴿Have they not journeyed through the land﴾, meaning: the disbelievers of your nation (ummah),

﴿and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ ﴿Allah destroyed them﴾, He annihilated them with a destruction of uprooting (istiʼsal),

﴿and for the disbelievers﴾, the polytheists of Quraysh,

﴿there are similar ones﴾, similar to that destruction, because the word "destroyed" (tadmir) indicates them.

﴿That﴾ i.e., the victory of the believers and the evil end of the disbelievers,

﴿because Allah is the Protector (mawla) of those who believe﴾, their Guardian (waliyy) and their Helper (nasir),

﴿and because the disbelievers have no protector (mawla) for them﴾, i.e., they have no helper for them. Allah is the Mawla of all servants in terms of origination (al-ikhtira') and possession of disposal over them, and He is the Mawla of the believers in particular in terms of support (al-nusra).

(p-325) ﴿Indeed, God admits those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow, while those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat﴾: they benefit from the provision of this worldly life for a few days.

﴿and eat﴾: heedless, not reflecting on the outcome.

﴿as cattle eat﴾: in their fodder and their pastures, heedless of what they are about to face, namely slaughter and butchering.

﴿and the Fire is their abode﴾: a place of descent and dwelling.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 13:

﴿And how many a town﴾ means: "How many a town!" It is for multiplication (of number), and by "the town" he means its people; for this reason He said: "We destroyed them,"

﴿which was mightier in strength than your town which has driven you out﴾ means: "And how many a town mightier in strength than your people who drove you out!" That is, they were the cause of your leaving,

﴿We destroyed them, and there was none to help them﴾ means: there was no one among them who would help them and ward off the punishment from them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 14:

﴿Is one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾ means: upon a proof from Him, and a demonstrative evidence (burhan), and this is the inimitable Qur'an and all the other miracles (mu'jizat), i.e., the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),

﴿like one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive﴾: they are the people of Mecca, for whom Satan made their polytheism (shirk) and their enmity toward Allah and His Messenger attractive. He said "the evil of his deeds" [in the singular],

﴿and they follow their desires﴾: [the plural here is] for the sake of conveying the meaning of "man" (man), after first conveying its wording (lafz).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 15:

﴿Mathal al-Jannah﴾ (the description of Paradise), the description of Paradise, which is of wondrous station,

﴿allatī wu'ida al-muttaqūn﴾ (which the God-fearing have been promised), from shirk (associating partners with God),

﴿fīhā anhārun﴾ (therein are rivers): this falls within the ruling of the relative clause (ṣilah), as a repetition of it. Do you not see the soundness of your saying, "allatī fīhā anhārun" (which has rivers therein)? Or it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: "established therein are rivers,"

﴿min mā'in ghayri āsin﴾ (of water unchanging): not changed in colour, smell or taste. It is said, "asina al-mā'" (the water became foul) when its taste and smell have changed. "Āsin" is read in the Meccan reading,

﴿wa-anhārun min labanin lam yataghayyar ṭa'muhu﴾ (and rivers of milk whose taste never changes), as the milk of this world changes into sourness and other things,

﴿wa-anhārun min khamrin ladhdhatin﴾ (and rivers of wine, a delight). The feminine of "ladhdh," which means delicious,

﴿lilshshāribīn﴾ (for drinkers). That is, it is nothing but pure enjoyment, with no loss of reason, no intoxication, no headache, and no other of the afflictions of wine,

﴿wa-anhārun min 'asalin muṣaffan﴾ (and rivers of honey, purified), not having come out of the bellies of bees, so that wax and other things would mix with it,

﴿wa-lahum fīhā (p-326) min kulli al-thamarāti wa-maghfiratun min rabbihim﴾ (for them therein is every kind of fruit and forgiveness from their Lord). "Mathal" is the subject, and its predicate is: ﴿kaman huwa khālidun fī al-nāri wa-suqū māan ḥamīman﴾ (like one who abides in the Fire and is given boiling water to drink), hot, at its extreme,

﴿fa-qaṭṭa'a am'a'ahum﴾ (so that it cuts up their bowels). The implied sense is: "Is the likeness of Paradise like the likeness of the recompense of one who abides in the Fire?!" This is a statement in the form of affirmation but its meaning is negation, because it is subsumed under the ruling of a statement introduced by the particle of denial, and enters within its scope, which is His saying: ﴿afaman kāna 'alā bayyinatin min rabbihi kaman zuyyina lahu sū'u 'amalihi﴾ [Muhammad: 14]. The purpose of omitting the particle of denial is to intensify the depiction of the obstinacy of one who equates those who hold to clear proof with those who follow their desires, and that it is as if he affirms equality between Paradise, in which those rivers flow, and the Fire, whose people are given boiling water to drink.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 16:

﴿And among them are some who listen to you, until, when they go out from your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?"﴾ They are the hypocrites (munafiqun). They would attend the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and hear his speech, but they would not retain it, nor give it any attention, out of contempt on their part. When they went out, they would say to the people of knowledge among the Companions, "What did he say just now?" in a mocking manner.

﴿They are those whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts, and who followed their own desires.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 17:

﴿And those who are guided﴾, by faith and by listening to the Qur'an,

﴿He increases﴾, Allah, ﴿them in guidance﴾, that is: insight and knowledge; or He expands their breasts,

﴿and gives them their piety﴾, He helps them to it; or He gives them the reward of their piety; or He makes clear to them what they should guard against.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 18:

﴿Are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly?﴾ That is: they are waiting (yantaziruna).

﴿That it should come upon them﴾ That is: its coming. So it is a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) for "the Hour" (al-sa'ah).

﴿Suddenly﴾: unexpectedly (faj'atan).

﴿Its signs have already come﴾: its marks (alamatuha). These are the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), the splitting of the moon, and the smoke. It has also been said: the severing of kinship ties, the scarcity of the noble, and the abundance of the base.

﴿How then for them, when their reminder comes to them?﴾ Al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash al-Awsat, a grammarian of Basra) said: the estimated (taqdir) reading is: "How will they have their reminder when it comes to them?!"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 47, verse 19:

﴿So know﴾, that it is the matter [of the case]:

﴿that there is no god but Allah. And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women﴾ (p-327). The meaning is: remain steadfast in what you already have of knowledge of Allah's oneness, and in humility and self-abasement, by seeking forgiveness for your sin and the sins of those who follow your religion. In *Sharh al-Ta'wilat* (an explanatory commentary on the *Ta'wilat*), it is said: it is permissible that he had a sin, so He commanded him to seek forgiveness for it, but we do not know it. However, the sin of the prophets is the abandonment of what is better, not the committing of what is ugly, whereas our sins are the committing of ugly deeds, both minor and major. It has also been said: the *fa'* (so) particles in these verses are for conjoining one sentence to another, with a connection between them.

﴿And Allah knows your moving about﴾, in your livelihoods and your trading,

﴿and your resting place﴾: He knows where you settle among your dwellings. Or, your moving about in your life and your resting place in the graves. Or, your moving about in your deeds and your resting place in Paradise and the Fire. Something like this is worthy of being feared, of being dreaded, and of being sought forgiveness for. Sufyan ibn Uyayna was asked about the excellence of knowledge, and he said: "Have you not heard His saying: ﴿So know that there is no god but Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾? So he was commanded to act after knowing."

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 47, verse 20:**

﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?"﴾, in which there is mention of jihad.

﴿But when a surah is sent down﴾, in the sense of jihad,

﴿clear (*muhkamah*)﴾, explicit, not ambiguous (*mutashabihah*), admitting no meaning except the obligation of fighting. From Qatadah: "Every surah in which fighting is mentioned is *muhkamah*, because abrogation (*naskh*, the replacement of one ruling by a later one) does not apply to it, since fighting abrogated what was of pardon and truce, and it has not been abrogated until the Day of Resurrection,"

﴿and fighting is mentioned in it﴾, meaning: it was commanded in it to fight,

﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, hypocrisy, meaning: you see the hypocrites among themselves becoming impatient with it,

﴿looking at you with the look of one fainting from death﴾, meaning: their eyes stare out of cowardice and dread, as one overtaken by a swoon at the approach of death looks.

﴿So woe to them﴾, a threat, in the sense of "woe to them." It is *afal*, from *al-wulyu*, which means nearness, and its meaning is a curse upon them that what is hateful should befall them.

Obedience and honorable speech (are better for them). This is a resumed statement; that is, obedience and honorable speech are better for them.

"And when the matter is resolved upon" (﴿فَإذا عَزَمَ الأمْرُ﴾): when the matter becomes serious, and the obligation of fighting (qital) falls upon them.

"Then if they had been true to Allah" (﴿فَلَوْ صَدَقُوا اللهَ﴾): in faith and obedience (p-328).

"It would have been better for them" (﴿لَكانَ﴾ ﴿خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾): the truthfulness would have been better for them than disliking jihad. Then he turned from the third person (ghayba) to the second person (khitab), with a kind of rebuke and warning, and said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 22:

﴿So is it possible that, if you turn away, you would cause corruption on the earth and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ Meaning: perhaps, if you turn away from the religion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his sunnah, you would return to what you were upon in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) of corruption on the earth, through mutual raids (taghawur) and plundering (tanahub), severing of kinship by fighting among relatives against one another, and burying of daughters alive. The predicate of "'asa" (ʿasā, "perhaps," a verb of approximation) is: "an tufsidu" (that you cause corruption). The conditional clause is a parenthetical insertion between the noun and the predicate, and the implied sentence is: "So is it possible that you would cause corruption on the earth and sever your ties of kinship, if you turn away?"

These are the ones whom Allah has cursed (﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ "those"): a demonstrative referring to those mentioned earlier.

﴿الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللهُ﴾ "Those whom Allah has cursed": He has removed them far from His mercy.

﴿فَأصَمَّهُمْ﴾ "So He has made them deaf": from hearing the admonition.

﴿وَأعْمى أبْصارَهُمْ﴾ "And made their sight blind": from seeing the path of guidance with their eyes.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 24:

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an﴾, so that they would recognize what it contains of admonitions, warnings, and threats against the disobedient, until they would not dare to commit sins. And "am" (أم, "or"), in ﴿Or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾, is taken in the sense of "bal" (بَلْ, "rather/but"), together with the interrogative hamza of confirmation (همزة التقرير), in order to register upon them that their hearts are locked, so that no remembrance can reach them. The word "hearts" is indefinite (نُكِّرَتِ) because what is intended is "upon hearts that are hard, whose condition in this respect is unspecified," and what is meant is some of the hearts, namely the hearts of the hypocrites. The "locks" are attributed to the "hearts" (أُضِيفَتِ الأقْفالُ إلى القُلُوبِ) because what is meant is the locks specific to them, namely the locks of disbelief, which have been shut tight so that they do not open, such as ar-rayn (الرَيْن, "rust/covering"), al-khatm (الخَتْم, "sealing"), and at-tab' (الطَبْع, "stamping/imprinting").

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 25:

﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them﴾ — i.e., the hypocrites, who returned to disbelief secretly, after the truth had become evident to them.

﴿Satan embellished﴾ — adorned [it] for them.

﴿for them﴾ — a clause consisting of a subject and predicate, which occupies the predicate position of "inna" (indeed), like the example: "Indeed Zayd, ʿAmr passed by him" (inna Zaydan ʿAmrun marra bihi).

﴿and he gave them respite﴾ — and he extended for them [their] hopes and wishes; and "wa-umlā" (read as passive by Abu ʿAmr), i.e., they were granted time and their lifespans were prolonged.

(p-329) ﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah had sent down﴾, i.e., the hypocrites said to the Jews: ﴿We will obey you in some of the matter﴾, i.e., in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ) and in holding back from supporting him,

﴿But Allah knows their secret counsel﴾, read as the verbal noun from "asarra" (to conceal). Ḥamzah, ʿAlī and Ḥafs read ﴿israrahum﴾; others read ﴿asrarahum﴾, the plural of "sirr" (secret).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 27:

﴿How then, when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ That is: how will they act then? And what will their stratagem be at that time?

[Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said:] "No one dies upon disobedience except that the angels strike him on his face and his back."

﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ [That] is a reference to the aforementioned taking of souls (al-tawaffi) described above,

﴿بِأنَّهُمُ﴾ [because they] means: because of the fact that they,

﴿اتَّبَعُوا ما أسْخَطَ اللهَ﴾ [followed that which angered God] — namely, aiding the disbelievers,

﴿وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ﴾ [and disliked His pleasure] — namely, supporting the believers,

﴿فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [so He made their deeds fruitless].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 29:

﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will never bring out their malice?﴾ — i.e., their rancor and grudges. The meaning is: "Do the hypocrites think that Allah (Exalted) will not expose their hatred and enmity towards the believers?!"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 30:

﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you﴾, i.e., We would have made them known to you and pointed them out to you,

﴿so you would have recognized them by their marks﴾, i.e., by their sign. This is that Allah marks them with a sign by which they are known. It is related from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "After this verse, none of the hypocrites remained hidden from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); he would recognize them by their marks." ﴿And you will surely recognize them by the tone of speech﴾, i.e., by its manner and its fine style, in the import of their words, because they were not able to conceal what was in their souls. The lam in "fa-la-ʿarafta-hum" (لَعَرَفْتَهُمْ) enters into the response of "law" (لَوْ), like the one in "la-arayna-kahum" (لَأرَيْناكَهُمْ), and it was repeated in the coordinated clause. As for the lam in "wa-la-taʿrifannahum" (وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ), it occurs together with the nun in the response of an omitted oath. (p-330) ﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾, so He distinguishes their good from their bad.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 32:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar (others) from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger﴾, and oppose him (ʿAdāwahu), meaning the feeders (al-Muṭʿimīn) on the Day of Badr, and this has already passed,

﴿after guidance has become clear to them﴾, after it became evident to them that it is the truth, and they recognized the Messenger,

﴿they will not harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds fruitless﴾, the deeds which they performed in opposing the Messenger. That is, He will nullify them, so they will not attain their aims through them.
O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds, [i.e., by hypocrisy or by showing off].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 34:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar [others] from the way of Allah, then die while they are disbelievers — never will Allah forgive them.﴾ It has been said: they are the people of the well (aṣḥāb al-qalīb), but the apparent meaning is general.

(p-331) ﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but play and amusement﴾: it is cut off in the briefest span of time.

﴿And if you believe﴾ in Allah and His Messenger,

﴿and fear Allah﴾, [i.e., avoid] shirk,

﴿He will give you your rewards﴾: the reward of your faith and your God-consciousness.

﴿And He will not ask you for your wealth﴾: that is, He will not ask you for all of it, but only a fortieth (rubʿ al-ʿushr). The subject of the verb is "Allah," or it may be "the Messenger."

Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna said: "a small portion of an abundance."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 37:

﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your resentments.﴾ That is: He would exert you and demand all of it. "Al-ihfa'" (persistent insistence) means exaggeration and reaching the utmost limit in anything. It is said: "ahfahu fi al-mas'alah" (he pressed him in the request) when he leaves out no part of importunity. And "ahfa sharibahu" (he shaved his moustache) means when he uprooted it entirely.

﴿you would be stingy, and He would bring out﴾: that is, God, or stinginess,

﴿your resentments﴾, at the time of refusal, or at the time of asking of everyone, because at the time of a request for wealth, enmity and rancor become apparent.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 38:

﴿Here you are﴾. "Ha" is for alerting (tanbih).

﴿These﴾ is a relative pronoun (mawsul) in the sense of "those who" (alladhina). Its relative clause (silah) is: ﴿are called﴾, meaning: you are those who are called.

﴿To spend in the way of Allah﴾: this is spending in the military campaign (ghazw), or zakat. It is as if he said: the proof that, if He pressed you, you would be stingy and dislike giving, is that you are called to pay a quarter of a tenth (rub' al-'ushr).

﴿Among you there are those who are stingy﴾, with the nominative (raf'), because "man" (who/some) here is not conditional. That is: among you are people who are stingy with it.

﴿And whoever is stingy﴾, with charity and the payment of the obligatory duty.

﴿Then he is only stingy against his own self﴾, meaning: he is stingy against the call of his own self, not against the call of his Lord. It was also said: he is stingy toward himself. One says "bakhiltu 'alayhi" and "bakhiltu 'anhu" (both are used).

﴿And Allah is the Rich, and you are the poor﴾, meaning: He does not command this out of need for it, because He is free of needs; rather it is for your need and your poverty toward reward.

﴿And if you turn away﴾, and if you, O Arabs, turn away from His obedience, the obedience of His Messenger, and spending in His way. It is coordinated (ma'tuf) with ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah﴾.

﴿He will substitute a people other than you﴾, He will create a people better than you and more obedient, and they are Persians (Fars). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about these people, while Salman was beside him. He struck his thigh and said: "This one and his people. By Him in whose hand my soul is, if faith were suspended at the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it." (p-332)

﴿Then they will not be like you﴾, meaning: then they will not be like you in obedience, but more obedient than you.
